thread:
infra-bot: INCIDENT PAGER triggered — KV cache spike detected in prod-region-us-west-2 (alert: kv_cache_key_count > 95th pct)

sarah.c: seeing huge mem & evictions on rope-kv-shard-12. latency climbs to 2.3s p95 for text-generation. stack traces show continuous-batching backlog + sliding-window NTK growth.

omar: confirmed. rolling token rate from a single customer looks like a sliding-window churn pattern. keys spiking per request due to longscroll/sliding-window keeping KV prefixes.

lee_oncall: paging in. taking ownership for initial mitigation. @sarah.c can you post the commands you want us to run?

sarah.c: first step — turn off the experimental sliding-window prefix retention for the model group. patch config:

```
# temporary hotfix
rope.features.sliding_window.enabled = false
continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens = 16384  # reduce from 65536
kv.cache.max_keys_per_prefix = 200  # throttle per-request key growth
```

sarah.c: pushing hotpatch to prod control plane now — will push canary then global if green.

deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix/disable-sliding-window -> canary-prod (rope-service). id: dep-98431

rajesh: notice a customer-exposed error 503 on a small subset of requests during canary. looks like canary nodes rejected some very large sequences.

lee_oncall: temporarily shifting traffic away from canary. scaling up kv-shards by +2 to give breathing room. running `infra scale kv-shard --add 2 --region us-west-2`.

omar: also enabling per-customer burst rate limiting to prevent single tenant from filling KV space.

emily-pm: which customers are impacted? we need to notify support and account teams.

sarah.c: affected customer bucket: prod-cust-742, and a handful of autoscaling test agents. major customers still serving but some experienced elevated latencies and transient 503s for long-context endpoints. estimated affected requests ~0.6% of traffic during spike window.

lee_oncall: mitigation checklist executed:
- sliding-window disabled (rolled back to 00:04)
- continuous_batching limits reduced and reloaded
- kv shard scale +2 completed at 1768802100
- per-prefix key throttle set
- flushed high-eviction prefixes on rope-kv-shard-12 (`kvctl flush --prefix longscroll-temp-`)

infra-bot: kv shard scaling finished: 2 new shards registered.

omar: after changes p95 latency dropped from 2.3s -> 420ms over 12 minutes. evictions down. continuous-batching queue depth reduced, token throughput steady.

rajesh: rolling back the canary deploy; we should keep sliding-window disabled until we do a full regression on staging with NTK and YaRN loads.

sarah.c: agreed. root cause hypothesis: rope scaling combined with long-context sliding-window keeps creating unique KV keys per sliding-window offset (NTK/YaRN interactions cause large prefix churn). continuous-batching config previously assumed amortized KV reuse; with sliding-window that assumption breaks and cache growth blows past shard memory planning.

emily-pm: action items for follow-up:
- post-incident postmortem draft (owner: emily-pm)
- repro harness on staging with synthetic NTK/YaRN sliding-window traffic (owner: sarah.c)
- add circuit-breaker to rope runtime to limit per-request prefix growth (owner: eng-runtime)
- add telemetry to surface per-prefix key churn in realtime (owner: eng-infra)
- customer comms draft for prod-cust-742 (owner: customer-success)

lee_oncall: handing off to day oncall @omar for monitoring and follow-up. I'll update the incident status to "mitigated but under review".

omar: ack. monitoring: watch kv_cache_key_count, kv_eviction_rate, continuous_batching.queue_depth, and generation_p95 for the next 6 hours. set alerts to lower thresholds for auto paging.

infra-bot: incident status updated -> MITIGATED (1768803000).

rajesh: note for postmortem: consider adding a safety clamp when rope.sliding_window is enabled: precompute expected key growth and disallow configs over shard capacity.

sarah.c: I'll start the staging repro this afternoon. putting up a draft for the rollback/hotfix runbook in #eng-runtime. includes commands we executed and exact config diffs.

emily-pm: good. support notified, customer-success reaching out to prod-cust-742. tagging this for an on-call review in tomorrow's morning sync. :white_check_mark:

lee_oncall: closing my handoff. leaving a short blameless note in incidents. thanks team. :pray:

omar: leaving watch for another 2h, will escalate if anything regresses.
